title: Administrative units: which users can a delegated administrator manage?
summary: The page overstates the protection provided by Purview administrative-unit scoping. Microsoft documents that overlapping Entra roles take precedence and give unscoped access, even when a scoped Purview assignment exists. The listed controls and licensing requirements are otherwise supported.

claims.claim: An administrative unit is an Entra ID container that can contain only users, groups or devices.
claims.quote: An administrative unit can contain only users, groups, or devices.

claims.claim: An Entra role assigned at administrative-unit scope reaches only that unit's members.
claims.quote: When a Microsoft Entra role is assigned at the scope of an administrative unit, role permissions apply only when managing members of the administrative unit itself, and don't apply to tenant-wide settings or configurations.

claims.where: summary; What it is: In Microsoft Purview; Why it matters
claims.claim: Assigning units to a Purview role-group member limits their policy management and visibility to users in those units without qualification.
claims.quote: If you assign both an Entra role and a scoped Microsoft Purview role group assignment to a user or group (for example, a role group scoped to an Administrative Unit), the Entra role takes precedence at runtime.
claims.fix: Replace the summary's second sentence with 'Unit-scoped roles delegate regional or departmental administration without tenant-wide rights.' Qualify the Purview scoping statement in What it is with: 'For overlapping capabilities, an Entra role takes precedence over a scoped Purview role-group assignment and gives unscoped access.' Apply that qualification to the corresponding statement in Why it matters. The qualification is documented under Role precedence and scope behavior at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions.
